biography: Philippe Prette, born under the Tuscan sun, is Italian motorsport royalty in the making. The son of a vineyard owner, Philippe's first taste of speed came not on the track, but tearing through the rolling hills of his family's estate on a souped-up quad bike. At 16, his father relented and bought him a kart. Within a year, he was dominating local championships. His raw talent attracted the attention of Bianco Audace, who swiftly signed him to their junior program. While a fiery crash at Monza in 2019 threatened to derail his career, Philippe bounced back stronger, showcasing incredible resilience and determination. Now, at 28, he is Bianco Audace's leading man, a symbol of Italian flair and racing excellence, hungry to prove himself at the highest level.
drivingStyle: Philippe's driving style is as flamboyant as his personality. He's an aggressive late-braker, often pushing the limits of the car and tires. He's known for his daring overtakes and his ability to extract maximum performance from the car in qualifying. While his aggressive style can sometimes lead to mistakes, it also makes him incredibly exciting to watch. Tire management isn't his strength, often resulting in late-race struggles, but his sheer pace and determination frequently compensate for this weakness.

rivalries.name: Jean-Pierre Dubois
rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at Le Mans in 2021, where Dubois accused Prette of deliberately running him off the track.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka's calm, calculated approach clashes directly with Prette's aggressive style, leading to intense on-track battles and a simmering rivalry for the 'fastest driver' title.

rivalries.name: Isabella Rossi
rivalries.reason: A fierce battle for the Bianco Audace team leader position, fueling intense competition both on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks (unwashed) for every race.
Listens to Italian opera at full volume right before entering the car.
Refuses to walk under ladders, even in the paddock.
famousQuote: "You either push the limit, or you get pushed aside."
careerHighlight: Winning the Italian Grand Prix at Monza in 2022 after starting from P8, showcasing his exceptional overtaking skills and never-say-die attitude.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2019 after a mechanical failure, costing his team a likely victory and leaving him with a broken collarbone.
